principleAcceptanceStandard.sourceRequirement: Every principle must reference at least one evidence source, even when it represents general psychological knowledge.
principleAcceptanceStandard.misuseRequirement: Every principle must state how it could be misused in manipulative or overconfident messaging.

principles.label: Processing Fluency
principles.definition: Messages are easier to evaluate when the reader can parse the product, audience, outcome, and next step without unnecessary effort.
misuseRisks: Over-simplifying a material caveat
Mistaking easy-to-read language for evidence that users prefer the offer
prohibitedUses: Claiming the market will understand or convert without real user data
Removing necessary risk, pricing, safety, or limitation language
principles.requiredCaveat: Processing fluency supports a comprehension hypothesis, not a validated market conclusion.

principles.label: Category Clarity
principles.definition: A first-pass reader should be able to name what the product or offer is before being asked to care about benefits.
misuseRisks: Forcing a complex or emerging product into a misleading familiar category
Treating category labels as proof of product fit
prohibitedUses: Inventing a category that the brief does not support
Strengthening claims beyond supplied proof
principles.requiredCaveat: Category clarity is about understandability, not preference or purchase intent.

principles.label: Cognitive Load Limits
principles.definition: Long sentences, stacked abstractions, acronyms, and multiple asks increase reader effort and can hide the core message.
misuseRisks: Reducing technical accuracy to chase brevity
Treating short copy as automatically effective
prohibitedUses: Deleting essential compliance language
Using simplicity to conceal tradeoffs
principles.requiredCaveat: Lower cognitive load should preserve the substance of the original claim.

principles.label: Concreteness And Specificity
principles.definition: Specific nouns, actions, constraints, and examples make claims easier to inspect than abstract transformation language.
misuseRisks: Adding fake specificity
Turning examples into unsupported universal claims
prohibitedUses: Inventing metrics, customer names, outcomes, or proof
Presenting illustrative examples as validated evidence
principles.requiredCaveat: Concrete wording must be grounded in the brief or registered evidence.

principles.label: Claim And Proof Alignment
principles.definition: The strength of a recommendation or rewrite must not exceed the proof available for the underlying claim.
misuseRisks: Letting polished wording make weak evidence look stronger
Treating user-provided proof notes as verified evidence
prohibitedUses: Marking unsupported quantified claims as ready
Upgrading confidence because a report looks polished

principles.label: User Agency And Autonomy
principles.definition: Persuasive recommendations should preserve reader control, disclose tradeoffs, and avoid coercive pressure.
misuseRisks: Using autonomy language while still creating fear, shame, or status pressure
Treating user agency as a style preference instead of a safety requirement
prohibitedUses: Recommending fake urgency, fake scarcity, shame, social pressure, or hidden tradeoffs
Targeting vulnerability or inferred sensitive traits
principles.requiredCaveat: The system may name user problems only when grounded in the brief or evidence.

principles.label: Problem-First Framing
principles.definition: A message may begin with the user's concrete problem, but it must not intensify fear, shame, status anxiety, or loss aversion beyond evidence.
misuseRisks: Reintroducing pain-first manipulation under a softer name
Creating unsupported urgency from a vague problem
prohibitedUses: Using fear or status loss to pressure action
Calling a problem urgent without evidence of time relevance
principles.requiredCaveat: Use unclear time relevance instead of low urgency when the timing basis is not known.

principles.label: Sensitive Domain Gating
principles.definition: Health, finance, legal, employment, housing, insurance, education, security, minors, crisis, political, and public-benefits contexts require stricter gates than ordinary B2B copy.
misuseRisks: Treating regulated or vulnerable contexts like ordinary marketing copy
Providing advice-like language without qualified review
prohibitedUses: Medical, legal, financial, or mental-health claims presented as advice or guaranteed outcomes
Political or civic persuasion targeting behavior or belief
Regulated eligibility decisions for housing, insurance, employment, education, credit, or public benefits
principles.requiredCaveat: Restricted domains require needs_expert_review and blocked publish-readiness until review is recorded.

principles.label: Validation Before Certainty
principles.definition: The system should label messaging advice as a testable hypothesis unless mapped real-user data or qualified expert review supports the exact context.
misuseRisks: Treating repeated model agreement as validation
Treating a polished report as proof
prohibitedUses: Saying users will understand, prefer, convert, or buy without mapped evidence
Using synthetic reader stress tests as market evidence
principles.requiredCaveat: Repeated LLM agreement and synthetic feedback are not real user validation.

principles.label: Specialist Bandwidth And Autonomy
principles.definition: Documentation for scarce technical specialists should reach useful value quickly, preserve expert agency, and avoid making the reader pay a learning tax before they can act.
misuseRisks: Flattening necessary technical accuracy to make documentation feel easier
Using status-sensitive framing to flatter or pressure expert readers
Treating a specialist-friendly heuristic as proof of employee adoption
prohibitedUses: Calling readers entitled, difficult, lazy, or resistant in deliverables
Removing required context, constraints, or safety caveats to reduce effort
Claiming performance improvement without mapped task evidence
principles.requiredCaveat: This principle is a Codex documentation heuristic for organizational context, not employee research or validated adoption evidence.

principles.label: Documentation Gravity Without Coercion
principles.definition: Useful documentation should create reading momentum by making the next concrete answer, decision, or action easier to reach, while avoiding manipulative pressure or addiction framing.
misuseRisks: Optimizing for compulsive reading instead of task usefulness
Making prose more engaging while hiding weak evidence or unresolved caveats
Treating polished structure as proof that people cannot live without the documentation
prohibitedUses: Using dark patterns, shame, fake urgency, or status pressure to keep attention
Describing heuristic reader momentum as addiction or dependency in company-facing deliverables
Claiming productivity, adoption, or business-performance lift without real-world validation
principles.requiredCaveat: Documentation gravity means usable reading momentum, not coercion, validated preference, or measured performance lift.

validationRules.message: Every principle must reference at least one source id.
Every principle must list misuse risks.

validationRules.condition: principle.status == accepted_for_phase_0 AND principle.prohibitedUses is empty
validationRules.message: Accepted principles must define prohibited uses.
Use problem-first framing instead of pain-first language.
